Buyer Added Bid Specific Scope Of Work(SOW) Text Clause(s) BUYER ADDED TENDER SPECIFIC TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS AND TERMS & CONDITIONS Description of Job: GPS-based Vehicle Tracking Service (GPS VTS) with virtual Geofencing for 17 vehicles 1. Scope of Service 1.1. The Service Provider shall provide GPS-based Vehicle Tracking Service (GPS VTS) with virtual Geofencing for 17 vehicles deployed at Tikak Colliery, NEC, for a period of 1 year. 1.2. The scope shall include GPS tracking devices, installation, commissioning, SIM connectivity, web-based d ashboard, software, map services, Geofencing, alerts, reports, data hosting, maintenance, technical support and integration with the existing ICCC platform of NEC/CIL. 1.3. The contract is for a complete vehicle tracking service and shall not be limited to the supply of standalon e GPS devices.

2. GPS Tracking Devices and Installation 2.1. The Service Provider shall supply, install, configure, test and commission GPS/GNSS tracking devices in a ll 17 designated vehicles. 2.2. The GPS/GNSS tracking devices shall be rugged and suitable for operation in coal-mine environments, inc luding dust, vibration, temperature variations and exposure to rain and water splashes. The device enclosure shall have a minimum ingress protection rating of IP67 in accordance with IS/IEC 60529. Compliance shall be supported by the manufacturer's datasheet or a test certificate from a competent testing laboratory. 2.3. The Service Provider shall maintain a vehicle-wise register of GPS tracking devices, including device IDs, vehicle registration numbers, SIM details, installation, replacement and maintenance records. The system sh all also maintain a dated audit trail of device replacement, deactivation/restoration, vehicle-device mapping c hanges and configuration changes, wherever applicable to the supplied platform. Records of relevant user/ad ministrator activities shall also be maintained and made available to authorised NEC officials upon request. 2.4. Installation, removal, transfer and reinstallation of devices shall be carried out in coordination with the a uthorized NEC representative. 3. SIM Connectivity and Network Services 3.1. The Service Provider shall provide active 4G/5G-compatible SIM connectivity and available mobile networ k, for all 17 vehicles. 3.2. The SIM cards shall be capable of providing reliable mobile data connectivity for transmission of GPS loca tion, vehicle movement, speed, status and other required tracking information to the VTS platform. 3.3. The Service Provider shall ensure adequate network coverage and connectivity for reliable operation of t he tracking system in the operational area of Tikak Colliery. 3.4. All SIM charges, data charges, SMS charges, network subscription charges and other recurring connectivi ty expenses shall be included in the quoted contract price. No additional payment shall be made by NEC on t his account. 3.5. The Service Provider shall monitor connectivity and take necessary corrective action in case of SIM failur e, network-related issues or interruption in data transmission. 3.6. Where technically supported, the system shall provide a suitable fallback mechanism, such as store-and- forward or SMS-based transmission, during temporary unavailability of mobile data connectivity. 4. Web-Based Dashboard and Live Tracking 4.1. The Service Provider shall provide a centralized web-based dashboard for authorized NEC officials to mo nitor all 17 vehicles. 4.2. The system shall display the latest available vehicle location, vehicle identification, speed, movement st atus and time of the last location update. 4.3. The system shall provide near real-time tracking of vehicle movement, route travelled and stoppages. Fo r moving vehicles, location updates shall be provided at intervals of 5–10sec and at intervals of up to 3 minut es when parked. Upon resumption of movement, tracking updates shall resume within 5–10 seconds. Horizon tal positional accuracy shall be less than 4 metres.

4.4. Authorized users shall be able to access the dashboard through commonly used web browsers. Mobile ac cess shall also be provided wherever supported by the offered solution. 5. Geofencing and Route Monitoring 5.1. The system shall support creation and configuration of virtual Geofences for the mine boundary, coal sto ckyards, weighbridges, loading/unloading points, workshops, parking areas and other locations as identified b y NEC. 5.2. The Service Provider shall configure the approved Geofence boundaries and routes in the VTS applicatio n based on the coordinates and instructions provided by the authorized NEC officials. 5.3. Any modification to approved Geofence boundaries or routes shall be carried out only on the instructions of the authorized NEC official and in accordance with the prescribed approval procedure. 5.4. The system shall generate alerts for Geofence entry/exit, unauthorized route deviation, overspeeding an d prolonged stoppage. 6. Alerts and Notifications 6.1. The system shall provide alerts for Geofence violations, route deviation, overspeeding, prolonged stoppa ge, device disconnection, GPS communication failure and tampering/power disconnection. 6.2. Alerts shall be available through the VTS dashboard and through SMS/e-mail or other supported notificati on mechanisms, as configured by NEC. 6.3. The system shall maintain event-wise records containing vehicle identification, date, time, event type an d available location details. 7. ICCC Integration 7.1. The GPS VTS shall be compatible and integrated with the existing ICCC platform of NEC/CIL. ICCC integrat ion shall be a mandatory deliverable under the contract. 7.2. The Service Provider shall coordinate with NEC and the authorized ICCC/system integrator to confirm the interface specifications, data fields, authentication requirements and integration procedure. 7.3. The Service Provider shall provide the necessary secure API/Web API or other interface approved by NEC for exchange of vehicle tracking data with the existing ICCC platform. 7.4. The integration shall provide vehicle identification, GPS coordinates, speed, direction, timestamp, vehicle status, Geofence events and route-deviation alerts. 7.5. Live vehicle locations shall be capable of display on the existing ICCC map/dashboard. Relevant alerts an d event data shall also be made available for display or processing in ICCC. 7.6. The Service Provider shall provide API documentation, data-field mapping, technical assistance and nece ssary support for integration testing and commissioning. Joint testing shall be carried out with the designated NEC/ICCC representatives to verify the agreed vehicle data, live location, vehicle status and alerts. Test resul ts and deficiencies, if any, shall be documented. The Service Provider shall rectify defects attributable to its GPS VTS solution or interface without additional cost and shall coordinate with the ICCC system integrator for resolution of integration issues involving the respective systems.

7.7. The Service Provider shall cooperate with the authorized ICCC integrator and rectify integration-related is sues attributable to its VTS solution during the contract period. 7.8. All basic API access, integration configuration, testing, commissioning and necessary technical support s hall be included in the quoted contract price. No separate integration or API charges shall be payable by NEC . 8. Reports and Historical Data 8.1. The system shall provide vehicle-wise and consolidated reports, as applicable, covering vehicle moveme nt, journey history, historical map playback, stoppages, Geofence violations, route deviation, over speeding, device connectivity status and system diagnostics 8.2. Reports shall be viewable online and downloadable in commonly usable formats such as Excel/CSV and P DF, as supported by the application. 8.3. Historical tracking and event data shall be retained for a minimum period of 12 months. 8.4. The Service Provider shall provide the required tracking data and reports in a commonly usable electroni c format upon request and upon expiry/termination of the contract, without additional cost. 9. Hosting, Data Security and Confidentiality 9.1. The Service Provider shall provide and maintain reliable server hosting, database, map services, backup and recovery facilities throughout the contract period. The hosting infrastructure shall incorporate server red undancy and automatic failover arrangements to minimise service disruption. The Service Provider shall mai ntain regular data backups and suitable recovery arrangements to prevent loss of tracking data. The data ce ntre hosting the contract-related data shall be located in India, subject to applicable CIL/NEC information sec urity policies and contractual requirements. 10. Maintenance and Technical Support 10.1. The Service Provider shall provide comprehensive preventive and corrective maintenance of GPS devic es, SIM connectivity, software, hosting and ICCC integration throughout the contract period as per GEM contr act. 10.2. The Service Provider shall provide a designated helpdesk/contact person and an escalation mechanism for reporting and resolving complaints. 10.3. Faulty devices shall be repaired or replaced within the response and resolution timelines specified in th e NIT/GeM Contract. 10.4. The Service Provider shall maintain suitable spare devices and components to minimize downtime and ensure continuity of tracking services. 10.5. Preventive maintenance, software/firmware updates and necessary configuration corrections shall be c arried out as required to maintain satisfactory service performance. 10.6. The Service Provider shall submit service reports covering complaints, repairs/replacements, device av ailability, preventive maintenance and ICCC integration status as required by NEC. 11. Commissioning and Acceptance

11.1. Commissioning shall include installation and activation of all 17 GPS tracking devices, vehicle mapping, dashboard access, verification of device specifications and supporting documents, Geofence configuration, al ert testing, report verification and joint testing of the specified ICCC integration. The integration test shall verify the agreed vehicle data, live location, vehicle status and alerts. The Service Provider shall rectify defici encies attributable to its supplied system without additional cost before acceptance by the designated NEC a uthority. 11.2. The Service Provider shall demonstrate the agreed functions to the designated NEC/ICCC representativ es and rectify deficiencies identified during testing without additional cost. 11.3. The service shall be considered commissioned upon acceptance by the designated NEC authority in acc ordance with the contractual requirements. 12. Payment and Deductions 12.1. Payment shall be made in accordance with the billing cycle and payment terms specified in the NIT and GeM Contract, subject to satisfactory service certification and submission of a valid invoice. 12.2. Deductions / LD If Service Provider fails to deliver any or all of the Service(s) or fail to perform the services within the time per iod specified in the Contract, the Buyer shall, without prejudice to its other rights and remedies under and in accordance with the Contract Agreement, levy Liquidated Damages (LD) from payments which are due to the Service Provider. Monitoring of Geofence violations and taking necessary operational/security action shall remain the res ponsibility of the designated NEC officials in accordance with the applicable CIL SOP. 14. Buyer Added Bid Specific Scope Of Work(SOW) Text Clause(s) BUYER ADDED TENDER SPECIFIC TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS AND TERMS & CONDITIONS Description of Job: GPS-based Vehicle Tracking Service (GPS VTS) with virtual Geofencing for 17 vehicles 1. Scope of Service 1.1. The Service Provider shall provide GPS-based Vehicle Tracking Service (GPS VTS) with virtual Geofencing for 17 vehicles deployed at Tikak Colliery, NEC, for a period of 1 year. 1.2. The scope shall include GPS tracking devices, installation, commissioning, SIM connectivity, web-based d ashboard, software, map services, Geofencing, alerts, reports, data hosting, maintenance, technical support and integration with the existing ICCC platform of NEC/CIL. 1.3. The contract is for a complete vehicle tracking service and shall not be limited to the supply of standalon e GPS devices.

2. GPS Tracking Devices and Installation 2.1. The Service Provider shall supply, install, configure, test and commission GPS/GNSS tracking devices in a ll 17 designated vehicles. 2.2. The GPS/GNSS tracking devices shall be rugged and suitable for operation in coal-mine environments, inc luding dust, vibration, temperature variations and exposure to rain and water splashes. The device enclosure shall have a minimum ingress protection rating of IP67 in accordance with IS/IEC 60529. Compliance shall be supported by the manufacturer's datasheet or a test certificate from a competent testing laboratory. 2.3. The Service Provider shall maintain a vehicle-wise register of GPS tracking devices, including device IDs, vehicle registration numbers, SIM details, installation, replacement and maintenance records. The system sh all also maintain a dated audit trail of device replacement, deactivation/restoration, vehicle-device mapping c hanges and configuration changes, wherever applicable to the supplied platform. Records of relevant user/ad ministrator activities shall also be maintained and made available to authorised NEC officials upon request. 2.4. Installation, removal, transfer and reinstallation of devices shall be carried out in coordination with the a uthorized NEC representative. 3. SIM Connectivity and Network Services 3.1. The Service Provider shall provide active 4G/5G-compatible SIM connectivity and available mobile networ k, for all 17 vehicles. 3.2. The SIM cards shall be capable of providing reliable mobile data connectivity for transmission of GPS loca tion, vehicle movement, speed, status and other required tracking information to the VTS platform. 3.3. The Service Provider shall ensure adequate network coverage and connectivity for reliable operation of t he tracking system in the operational area of Tikak Colliery. 3.4. All SIM charges, data charges, SMS charges, network subscription charges and other recurring connectivi ty expenses shall be included in the quoted contract price. No additional payment shall be made by NEC on t his account. 3.5. The Service Provider shall monitor connectivity and take necessary corrective action in case of SIM failur e, network-related issues or interruption in data transmission. 3.6. Where technically supported, the system shall provide a suitable fallback mechanism, such as store-and- forward or SMS-based transmission, during temporary unavailability of mobile data connectivity. 4. Web-Based Dashboard and Live Tracking 4.1. The Service Provider shall provide a centralized web-based dashboard for authorized NEC officials to mo nitor all 17 vehicles. 4.2. The system shall display the latest available vehicle location, vehicle identification, speed, movement st atus and time of the last location update. 4.3. The system shall provide near real-time tracking of vehicle movement, route travelled and stoppages. Fo r moving vehicles, location updates shall be provided at intervals of 5–10sec and at intervals of up to 3 minut es when parked. Upon resumption of movement, tracking updates shall resume within 5–10 seconds. Horizon tal positional accuracy shall be less than 4 metres.

4.4. Authorized users shall be able to access the dashboard through commonly used web browsers. Mobile ac cess shall also be provided wherever supported by the offered solution. 5. Geofencing and Route Monitoring 5.1. The system shall support creation and configuration of virtual Geofences for the mine boundary, coal sto ckyards, weighbridges, loading/unloading points, workshops, parking areas and other locations as identified b y NEC. 5.2. The Service Provider shall configure the approved Geofence boundaries and routes in the VTS applicatio n based on the coordinates and instructions provided by the authorized NEC officials. 5.3. Any modification to approved Geofence boundaries or routes shall be carried out only on the instructions of the authorized NEC official and in accordance with the prescribed approval procedure. 5.4. The system shall generate alerts for Geofence entry/exit, unauthorized route deviation, overspeeding an d prolonged stoppage. 6. Alerts and Notifications 6.1. The system shall provide alerts for Geofence violations, route deviation, overspeeding, prolonged stoppa ge, device disconnection, GPS communication failure and tampering/power disconnection. 6.2. Alerts shall be available through the VTS dashboard and through SMS/e-mail or other supported notificati on mechanisms, as configured by NEC. 6.3. The system shall maintain event-wise records containing vehicle identification, date, time, event type an d available location details. 7. ICCC Integration 7.1. The GPS VTS shall be compatible and integrated with the existing ICCC platform of NEC/CIL. ICCC integrat ion shall be a mandatory deliverable under the contract. 7.2. The Service Provider shall coordinate with NEC and the authorized ICCC/system integrator to confirm the interface specifications, data fields, authentication requirements and integration procedure. 7.3. The Service Provider shall provide the necessary secure API/Web API or other interface approved by NEC for exchange of vehicle tracking data with the existing ICCC platform. 7.4. The integration shall provide vehicle identification, GPS coordinates, speed, direction, timestamp, vehicle status, Geofence events and route-deviation alerts. 7.5. Live vehicle locations shall be capable of display on the existing ICCC map/dashboard. Relevant alerts an d event data shall also be made available for display or processing in ICCC. 7.6. The Service Provider shall provide API documentation, data-field mapping, technical assistance and nece ssary support for integration testing and commissioning. Joint testing shall be carried out with the designated NEC/ICCC representatives to verify the agreed vehicle data, live location, vehicle status and alerts. Test resul ts and deficiencies, if any, shall be documented. The Service Provider shall rectify defects attributable to its GPS VTS solution or interface without additional cost and shall coordinate with the ICCC system integrator for resolution of integration issues involving the respective systems.

7.7. The Service Provider shall cooperate with the authorized ICCC integrator and rectify integration-related is sues attributable to its VTS solution during the contract period. 7.8. All basic API access, integration configuration, testing, commissioning and necessary technical support s hall be included in the quoted contract price. No separate integration or API charges shall be payable by NEC . 8. Reports and Historical Data 8.1. The system shall provide vehicle-wise and consolidated reports, as applicable, covering vehicle moveme nt, journey history, historical map playback, stoppages, Geofence violations, route deviation, over speeding, device connectivity status and system diagnostics 8.2. Reports shall be viewable online and downloadable in commonly usable formats such as Excel/CSV and P DF, as supported by the application. 8.3. Historical tracking and event data shall be retained for a minimum period of 12 months. 8.4. The Service Provider shall provide the required tracking data and reports in a commonly usable electroni c format upon request and upon expiry/termination of the contract, without additional cost. 9. Hosting, Data Security and Confidentiality 9.1. The Service Provider shall provide and maintain reliable server hosting, database, map services, backup and recovery facilities throughout the contract period. The hosting infrastructure shall incorporate server red undancy and automatic failover arrangements to minimise service disruption. The Service Provider shall mai ntain regular data backups and suitable recovery arrangements to prevent loss of tracking data. The data ce ntre hosting the contract-related data shall be located in India, subject to applicable CIL/NEC information sec urity policies and contractual requirements. 10. Maintenance and Technical Support 10.1. The Service Provider shall provide comprehensive preventive and corrective maintenance of GPS devic es, SIM connectivity, software, hosting and ICCC integration throughout the contract period as per GEM contr act. 10.2. The Service Provider shall provide a designated helpdesk/contact person and an escalation mechanism for reporting and resolving complaints. 10.3. Faulty devices shall be repaired or replaced within the response and resolution timelines specified in th e NIT/GeM Contract. 10.4. The Service Provider shall maintain suitable spare devices and components to minimize downtime and ensure continuity of tracking services. 10.5. Preventive maintenance, software/firmware updates and necessary configuration corrections shall be c arried out as required to maintain satisfactory service performance. 10.6. The Service Provider shall submit service reports covering complaints, repairs/replacements, device av ailability, preventive maintenance and ICCC integration status as required by NEC. 11. Commissioning and Acceptance

11.1. Commissioning shall include installation and activation of all 17 GPS tracking devices, vehicle mapping, dashboard access, verification of device specifications and supporting documents, Geofence configuration, al ert testing, report verification and joint testing of the specified ICCC integration. The integration test shall verify the agreed vehicle data, live location, vehicle status and alerts. The Service Provider shall rectify defici encies attributable to its supplied system without additional cost before acceptance by the designated NEC a uthority. 11.2. The Service Provider shall demonstrate the agreed functions to the designated NEC/ICCC representativ es and rectify deficiencies identified during testing without additional cost. 11.3. The service shall be considered commissioned upon acceptance by the designated NEC authority in acc ordance with the contractual requirements. 12. Payment and Deductions 12.1. Payment shall be made in accordance with the billing cycle and payment terms specified in the NIT and GeM Contract, subject to satisfactory service certification and submission of a valid invoice. 12.2.
